A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeMe framework. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite the changed title, layout, and numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original DDPM and Stable Diffusion experiments, including FID/CLIP results, component ablations, sensitivity studies, and generated images.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and reports additional baseline comparisons in Tables 1, 2, and 4.

M1.justification: The timestep partitioning, separate finetuning, consistency loss, probabilistic sampling, channel-wise projection, and weighted task-vector merging remain unchanged. Expanded descriptions of merging search and projection size do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR10, LSUN-Church, and LSUN-Bedroom for unconditional generation, and LAION-Aesthetics finetuning with COCO, ImageNet1K, and PartiPrompts evaluation. The added comparisons use retained datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 add P2 Weighting, ANT-NashMTL, and ANT-UW alongside the retained loss-weighting baselines. New supplementary Table 4 compares against OMS-DPM and DiffPruning, substantially expanding the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: New Table 4 introduces comparisons across OMS-DPM time budgets and DiffPruning's 50% and 70% pruning settings, with model-count and parameter-count metrics. Existing benchmark splits, finetuning budgets, samplers, and FID/CLIP protocols remain unchanged. Newly disclosed search settings belong to D1.

E4.justification: The component ablation, N/p sensitivity studies, gradient and activation diagnostics, loss landscapes, task-vector analyses, and qualitative cases are retained. The LSUN examples are relocated, and the new expert-method comparison adds benchmark comparisons rather than a new ablation or robustness study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests for the performance results. Added comparisons retain the existing single-score reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 4 add substantial comparator results while retaining existing DeMe scores. New Table 2 entries change relative standings: merged DeMe's ImageNet FID remains 27.23, versus 26.92 for P2 Weighting and 26.91 for ANT-UW. Section 4.4 also corrects the incremental consistency-loss FID reduction from 0.13 to 0.05, without changing Table 3's values.

T1.justification: v2 removes Proposition 1 and Appendix A.3's proof that DeMe enables escape from a critical point; they are not relocated. The loss-reweighting derivations remain in Sections 7.1–7.2, with an added P2 Weighting objective and its conversion between prediction targets.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims about timestep-specific finetuning, merging without additional inference costs, improved generation across six benchmarks, and potential multi-task applications. The new title foregrounds a multi-task interpretation already explicit in v1.

C2.justification: Section 8 newly acknowledges exponential coefficient-search cost and explains the smaller sample used for candidate evaluation. Section 11 interprets the new expert-method comparison through single-model efficiency while acknowledging that the approaches are not directly related. Existing gradient-conflict and knowledge-sharing explanations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds code links, documents FID-based coefficient search using 5K images and coarse-to-fine steps, and supplies gradient-similarity measurement and projection-size details. These are disclosures about existing procedures. Training hyperparameters and hardware remain, but the explicit Stable Diffusion v1.4 identifier is dropped.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds P2 Weighting, DMP, DTR, and Switch-DiT with a limited expansion of the multi-task discussion. Several v1 bibliography entries, including Diffusion Soup, MaxFusion, and LCSC, disappear despite retained supplementary discussion, leaving unresolved citations. The central positioning around merging timestep-specialized models remains.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, reorders the channel-projection explanation, adds an acknowledgement, and reorganizes lettered appendices into numbered supplementary sections. Some qualitative discussion moves to the supplement, but most prose and the main section sequence remain closely matched.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted from one column to two, with resized, rearranged, and partly redrawn figures. Tables 1–2 gain rows, Table 4 is added, and the main-text LSUN figure moves to the supplement. These substantially alter visual presentation while retaining the qualitative examples.

improvement.justification: The added P2/ANT comparisons better test DeMe's positioning against loss-weighting and multi-task approaches, while the search details and code links improve reproducibility. These provide a modest net benefit. Gains are tempered by the removal of formal critical-point analysis, broken supplementary citations, and unchanged superiority wording that does not address merged DeMe's ImageNet FID disadvantage against newly added baselines.
